title: Perfect Eye: Perfect Dark and GoldenEye 007 run natively on PS5
summary: Perfect Eye brings Perfect Dark and GoldenEye 007 to PS5 as two separate home screen tiles, running natively on Vulkan at up to 4K with online multiplayer alongside PC players.
body: Perfect Eye by thesmokesession-bit is a native PS5 build of Dab's Mod (a fork of the Perfect Dark PC port) that also runs GoldenEye 007 on its own tile. Both games draw with the Vulkan renderer on Mihawk's RADV port at the TV's native resolution — up to 3840×2160 on a 4K set. Online play with PC users works through Dab's Mod lobby system with room codes, co-op, counter-op and kill cams. HD texture packs are supported for both games, and GoldenEye can use the Xbox 360 XBLA version's HD assets.

You need your own Perfect Dark (USA Rev 1) and GoldenEye 007 (USA) ROMs — no game data is included. Install via FTP to /data/homebrew/ on a jailbroken PS5 with etaHEN and ShadowMountPlus. The GoldenEye tile needs both ROMs since it runs on the Perfect Dark engine. RecompStore v1.1.3 also lists both games for one-click installation.

title: ps5-m2unmount: keep your M.2 clean between Linux sessions
summary: A new PS5 payload unmounts the console's M.2 SSD volume after jailbreak, preventing the "Repairing" screen that follows every PS5-Linux session.
body: The ps5-m2unmount payload by shcheglovnd solves a long-standing annoyance for PS5-Linux users: the console marks its M.2 volume dirty at every boot, and since ps5-linux-loader enters Linux through rest mode the volume is never cleanly unmounted, triggering a repair on the next PS5 boot. This payload unmounts the M.2 right after jailbreak and stays resident to re-unmount if the console remounts it later.

The payload uses kernel filesystem event filters (EVFILT_FS) rather than polling, so it does no periodic work while games run — it wakes only on mount/unmount events. It survives rest mode, never forces an unmount on a busy volume, and loading it again replaces the running copy. Tested on firmware 4.50 on a CFI-1115A. Send m2unmount.elf to an ELF loader on port 9021.

title: SoundBridge: stream PS5 game audio to your PC headset
summary: SoundBridge is a new PS5 payload and Windows app that streams game audio over the network to your PC with about 50 ms delay — no Remote Play or capture card required.
body: SoundBridge by Xnos666 sends your PS5's game sound to a small Windows app over the home network. If your PS5 is on a monitor without speakers and your headset is plugged into your PC (for example through a Focusrite Scarlett), the PS5's audio has nowhere to go — SoundBridge fixes that. Measured delay is about 50–55 ms over Wi-Fi, less with Ethernet. Two modes are available: Low Delay for minimum latency, and Smooth for a small buffer that rides out Wi-Fi pauses.

The PC app (native Direct2D, about 250 KB, no install) finds the PS5 by itself using auto-discovery. Send the ELF to your PS5 loader on port 9021 and the app turns green. The payload runs alongside other payloads and sending it again replaces the running copy. Tested on firmware 13.60 only.

title: PS5SX2 2.15: game tiles on the home screen, 192 more HD texture packs
summary: PS5SX2 2.15 (build vk-285-177) adds per-game home screen tiles, 192 new HD texture packs from the community Drive, less disc stutter, and frame generation at 120 Hz again.
body: PS5SX2 2.15 rolls up six test builds (172–177) into one stable release. The headline feature is game tiles: press Square on a game in the shelf and choose "Home screen tile" to get a dedicated tile on the PS5 home that launches the game directly. The shelf now offers 228 HD texture packs for 223 games from the community Google Drive, and covers gain back covers (flip with the right stick), spines, and disc art from the LaunchBox Games Database. Disc performance is improved — the game no longer waits on the drive, and reads ahead at 3.2× speed.

Frame generation can switch the TV to 120 Hz again, so a 60 fps game shows 120 — still off by default, needing a 120 Hz TV and "120 Hz Output" enabled. Folder settings are now exact: once you set a game, BIOS or textures folder, only that folder is scanned. Search the shelf with R2. Requires a jailbroken PS5 with ShadowMountPlus.

title: RetroArch v4.0.0-beta-4: play games over SMB, frame generation fixed
summary: PS5 RetroArch v4.0.0-beta-4 adds SMB network play from a shared PC folder, fixes the doubled-picture frame generation bug, and brings GameCube texture pack support.
body: RetroArch v4.0.0-beta-4 answers a stack of community bug reports. The biggest addition is SMB support: play games straight from a shared folder on your PC, configured through the WebUI. Frame generation no longer produces a doubled picture — the extra frames are now properly interleaved. GameCube texture packs that previously never showed up now work after a fix to Dolphin's memory path. The PSP core no longer crashes when changing resolution in the Quick Menu.

Other fixes include persistent renames, proper game removal, and a RetroAchievements password that no longer appears lost. The WebUI Update button now lights up correctly after releases gained the checksum file the updater needs. Update through the WebUI or download from the release page. Requires a jailbroken PS5.

title: Playden v0.5.0: Direct3D 12 games now run — Cyberpunk 2077 on PS5
summary: Playden v0.5.0 brings DirectX 12 game support through vkd3d-proton, making Cyberpunk 2077, Deep Rock Galactic and more playable on a jailbroken PS5.
body: Playden v0.5.0 adds vkd3d-proton via runtime kit 0.11, enabling Direct3D 12 games on the PS5 for the first time. Cyberpunk 2077, Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection, Deep Rock Galactic and more now run through Wine on the console. This release also adds sign-in with an account name and password, a setting for slow downloads, and an Installed Games list for freeing up storage space.

Updating from 0.4.0: Playden offers the update on next launch or from Settings › About. Make sure the console has at least 8 GB free before updating — the new kit unpacks next to the old one. Your sign-in, games, saves and game settings are kept, and prepared games update their runtime the next time you press Play. Alpha software: Playden signs in to your real Steam account.

title: PS5 Upload v7.1.7–v7.1.9: file properties, remote server organizer, better Kraken
summary: Three PS5 Upload updates in one day: v7.1.7 organizes packages on remote servers, v7.1.8 fixes Kraken decompression, and v7.1.9 adds file properties and custom permissions.
body: PS5 Upload v7.1.9 adds a Properties panel in Files showing size, modification time and permissions for any file or folder, with the ability to set custom Unix permissions. Settings now lets you show, restore or hide the PS5Upload Minion home screen tile through a paired connection even when LAN access is off. Cheat imports from local JSON trainers are supported. v7.1.8 fixes Kraken decompression for PS5 packages compressed at the highest level that previously errored with "chunk too short".

v7.1.7 extends the Organize Packages feature to remote SMB, FTP, SFTP and WebDAV servers — same preview, same Game ID layout, all runs undoable. WebDAV servers that redirect folder addresses (like Apache) work again. Download each version from the release page or update from within the app.

title: PatchDL v0.3.1–v0.3.2: faster downloads, choose your storage drive
summary: PatchDL v0.3.1 speeds up downloads by buffering writes, and v0.3.2 lets you pick which drive to save to — internal or any connected USB. Tested on firmware 11.60.
body: PatchDL v0.3.1 fixes a performance bottleneck: previously every small chunk was written to disk immediately, and the PS5's storage overhead capped speeds at 8–12 MB/s. Chunks are now collected in memory before flushing, significantly improving download throughput. v0.3.2 adds drive selection in Settings — it lists internal storage and every connected USB drive with free space, and new downloads go to whichever you choose.

The PatchDL tile now sits in the Media section of the home screen alongside other homebrew apps, and existing tiles move there automatically on the next launch. Both versions are tested on firmware 11.60 with USB drives. Send the ELF to your PS5 loader and open the address from the notification. PatchDL downloads official, unmodified game updates only.

title: Payload Manager v0.6.2: autoload return, release notes, smaller ELF
summary: Payload Manager v0.6.2 adds a Return After Autoload option, in-app release notes for payloads, and cuts the ELF size by moving emoji to a CDN. v0.6.3 hotfixes emoji display.
body: Payload Manager v0.6.2 brings several quality-of-life improvements. Return After Autoload is a new optional setting that sends you back to the dashboard about 3 seconds after all payloads load successfully — results stay visible if anything fails. A new Release Details section on payload pages shows GitHub release notes directly in the app. Dashboard icons can now be hidden for a text-focused layout, and Traditional Chinese and Romanian translations are added.

Under the hood, bundled emoji artwork has been replaced with Twemoji loaded from a CDN, significantly reducing the ELF size. Downloaded emoji are cached for offline use. Mobile upload controls are fixed for portrait mode. v0.6.3 is a hotfix for emoji not appearing on PS5. Update from within the Payload Manager app — the old ELF file automatically launches the updated version.

title: PS5 Home Assistant v0.2.0: rest mode and power off from Home Assistant
summary: PS5 Home Assistant v0.2.0 adds Rest Mode and Power Off buttons controllable from Home Assistant, an IP address sensor, and fixes the device going unavailable after rest mode wake.
body: PS5 Home Assistant v0.2.0 adds power control to the MQTT bridge. Rest Mode and Power Off buttons (off by default, enabled with power_actions in the config) beep the controller, show a notification, mark the device offline and use the system's own services. Each button requires a press and allows at most one action per 10 seconds. A new IP address diagnostic sensor keeps its last value while the console sleeps.

A bug where the device stayed unavailable in Home Assistant after waking from rest mode is fixed — the payload now publishes an online state with every update to counteract the broker's last-will offline message from the broken connection. Note that Power Off ends the jailbreak, and waking from Home Assistant is not possible on a jailbroken console. v0.2.1 renames the process to ps5-hass.elf so it shows correctly in payload manager lists.

title: PSBox Cloud Gaming v1.3.0: instant startup and one-click free game claims
summary: PSBox v1.3.0 renders the library from local cache for sub-150 ms startup, doubles DualSense polling to 250 Hz for lower input lag, and adds native one-click claiming of free-to-play games.
body: PSBox Cloud Gaming v1.3.0 brings major performance work validated on PS5 hardware. The app now renders its library from local cache on the first frame for under 150 ms startup time, with HTTP connection pooling eliminating repeated TLS handshakes. The DualSense polling rate is doubled from 125 Hz to 250 Hz, cutting input latency by half (~4 ms) with zero heap allocations. The RTP video receiver uses a pre-allocated ring buffer of 2048 slots, removing thousands of per-second memory allocations during streaming.

Free-to-play games like Fortnite and Roblox now show a native "Get Free" button on their detail screen instead of requiring a QR code, enabling one-click claiming directly from the console. Account saving is more robust, and Xbox Live error handling is improved. Update from the release page.

title: Jobee'sLair v0.4.1: now installs alongside Overdrive
summary: Jobee'sLair v0.4.1 gets its own app ID so it can be installed next to Overdrive — the two previously shared an ID and couldn't coexist.
body: Jobee'sLair v0.4.1 fixes a conflict where the app shared the same PS5 app ID as Overdrive, meaning only one could be installed at a time — the console treated them as the same app. Jobee'sLair now has its own unique ID. This is a manual update: copy the new JobeesLair.exfat over the old one in homebrew/, then open it. The in-app updater can't cross this change.

Your download list and play time carry over, but settings, favorites, feeds and your TorBox API key start fresh and need to be set up again. The old home screen icon can be deleted. From v0.4.1 onward, future updates can use the in-app Download and Install dialog or automatic updates in Settings → About.

title: RecompStore v1.1.3: more zip formats, Perfect Eye and Ninja Gaiden join the store
summary: RecompStore v1.1.3 handles more release zip layouts, adding Perfect Dark, GoldenEye 007 and Ninja Gaiden II to the store's installable games.
body: RecompStore v1.1.3 improves how release zips are unpacked. Some ports put their game folder one level deep in the zip or ship two games in one archive — like Perfect Eye, which contains both Perfect Dark and GoldenEye 007. The store now identifies and installs the folder matching the game's title ID and skips the rest. This brings Perfect Dark, GoldenEye 007, and Ninja Gaiden II into the store.

Already have RecompStore? Open it and update from Latest Updates. For a new install, send RecompStore-Installer.elf to port 9021. ShadowMountPlus puts the store on the home screen. Requires kstuff and ShadowMountPlus 1.7 Beta 5 or newer. No game files are included — every game needs your own legally obtained copy.

title: ProsperoStore v1.000.101–v1.000.102: shared-ID app support
summary: ProsperoStore v1.000.101 adds support for applications that share the same app ID, with v1.000.102 following as a CI fix.
body: ProsperoStore v1.000.101 resolves an issue where apps sharing the same PS5 app ID could conflict during installation. The store now handles shared-ID applications correctly. v1.000.102 is a maintenance release that fixes the release workflow.
Update from within ProsperoStore or download from the release page. ProsperoStore is the install client for the homebrew.page catalog.

title: DBZ Budokai 3: Dragon Ball Z runs natively on PS5 as an Xbox 360 recomp
summary: Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 3 from the HD Collection is now a native PS5 homebrew app, recompiled from the Xbox 360 version with the ReXGlue SDK.
body: A new PS5 homebrew app by elripalda brings Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 3 from the Budokai HD Collection to the console as native code. It builds on NovaPowers’ DBZ Budokai 3 HD Collection recomp and the ReXGlue SDK, drawing on Vulkan via Mesa RADV — no emulation involved. The app opens on a DualSense-native hub with PlayStation button prompts and includes trophies.

Installation is straightforward with RecompStore or by FTP. Copy your own Xbox 360 disc image into the app’s Assets folder and press Start Game. The hub checks that all files are present before launching. Requires a jailbroken PS5 running homebrew from /data/homebrew/ with ShadowMountPlus.

title: NFS Most Wanted (2005): the Black Box classic runs at 4K on PS5
summary: EA Black Box’s Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005) now runs as a PS5 homebrew app at 4K, with the PC version running through prospero-win and optional Xbox 360 visuals.
body: The nfs-blackbox-ps5 project by lavavex packages EA Black Box’s NFS Most Wanted (2005) as a native PS5 homebrew app. It runs the PC version through prospero-win at 4K resolution and includes quality-of-life mods: Widescreen Fix, DualSense support via XtendedInput (with touchpad as cursor), DSOAL audio, and an in-game PS5 Options menu for a performance overlay and settings. An optional Xbox 360 Stuff Pack adds the 360’s visuals, movies, HD reflections and front-end shadows.

You supply your own copy of the PC game (version 1.2 or 1.3) via FTP or USB; a 1.2 copy is patched to 1.3 during installation. The app installs and mods the game without modifying the original. Tested on a PS5 Pro on firmware 13.60 with etaHEN, kstuff and ShadowMount+. Install takes about three minutes with the Xbox 360 look enabled on a wired connection.

title: ps5-homeassistant: turn your PS5 into a Home Assistant device
summary: A new payload publishes PS5 temperatures, power draw, fan speed, frame rate and game info over MQTT, adding the console as a device in Home Assistant with notification and light control.
body: Marice’s ps5-homeassistant is a payload that runs alongside ps5-exporter and ps5-signal to publish the console’s telemetry over MQTT with Home Assistant auto-discovery. A "PS5" device appears automatically in Home Assistant with sensors for temperature, SoC and memory power, GPU clock, fan speed, CPU load, frame rate, current game, uptime and free space. Home Assistant can also send notifications to the TV (with emoji and its own icon), beep the controller, blink the light bar or change its colour.

Install the Mosquitto broker add-on in Home Assistant, create a user for the console, and load the ELF via your loader or ps5-autoloader. Configure the broker address through Signal Companion’s Payloads screen or a local API call. The payload talks plain MQTT on the home network, stores its config with owner-only permissions, and its local API only answers on 127.0.0.1. Requires a jailbroken PS5 with ps5-exporter 0.3.0 or later.

title: PS5 Upload v7.1.5: bulk uploads fixed, Files renamed to Minion
summary: PS5 Upload v7.1.5 fixes uploads of many small files getting stuck, renames PS5Upload Files to PS5Upload Minion, and patches payload catalog display issues.
body: PS5 Upload v7.1.5 fixes a bug where uploading many small files would stall after about 30 files with a "the console is busy" message. The console now releases each finished upload so every file goes through — a 240-file, 347 MB folder uploaded in about 2 minutes 20 seconds in testing. The companion app PS5Upload Files is now renamed to PS5Upload Minion; the home-screen tile picks up the new name the next time the helper starts.

The payload catalog also gets fixes: websrv’s newest release showed an error instead of the release because its notes are empty, and payloads whose GitHub page has been taken down (such as Ghostpad) now say so plainly while still offering the saved version. Time displays now read like "saved 3 days ago" instead of a raw second count.

title: ProsperoStore v1.000.100: detects running apps by sandbox entry
summary: ProsperoStore v1.000.100 now detects a running app by its app0 sandbox entry, a community contribution by andrescera.
body: ProsperoStore v1.000.100 adds detection of whether a homebrew app is currently running by checking its app0 sandbox entry. This is a community contribution by andrescera — their first to the project. The detection lets the store show whether an installed app is active before you try to manage or update it.

ProsperoStore is the on-console front-end for the homebrew.page catalog, letting you browse, install and update PS5 homebrew apps directly from the console. Requires a jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader.

title: VLC v0.4.6: hardware decoding toggle fix and archive handling
summary: VLC v0.4.6 fixes re-enabling hardware decoding on a paused live channel and stops archives on network shares from playing as video files.
body: VLC v0.4.6 for PS5 fixes two bugs. Turning hardware decoding back on after disabling it didn’t take effect on a paused live channel until you opened it again — this now applies immediately. Zip, RAR and 7z archive files stored on a network share were incorrectly played as video instead of being opened as folders.
VLC is the PS5 port of the VideoLAN media player, supporting local, USB and network playback with hardware-accelerated decoding. Requires a jailbroken PS5.

title: Jobee’sLair v0.4.0: complete translations and faster catalog search
summary: Jobee’sLair v0.4.0 completes all 13 language translations, speeds up catalog search and filters, adds a startup animation and a debug log.
body: Jobee’sLair v0.4.0 is a stability release that finishes the app’s localization: all 13 language translations now cover every screen, where previously about half the app fell back to English. Catalog search and filter operations do roughly a third of the work they used to, and source-list ranking is cut in half. A new startup animation shows sparks spiraling into the JL logo before the store fades in, and the version number is now always visible under the logo.

The release also adds a debug log at /data/ps5-react/PPSA99058/logs/jobeeslair.log, readable over FTP, which stays under about 1 MB and blanks out API keys, tokens and email addresses. A browser-capture failure now shows the real reason instead of a generic message. For developers, tests now run with npm test and npm run test:render, and check every language’s string completeness and placeholder correctness on every push.

title: PS5-Suite v7.6.0: trophy unlocking for next-gen SDK titles and per-save icons
summary: PS5-Suite v7.6.0 unlocks trophies in UDS-driven games like Onimusha: Way of the Sword, shows per-save icons, and fixes a power-sensor buffer overflow.
body: PS5-Suite v7.6.0 adds trophy support for next-gen SDK titles that use libSceNpUniversalDataSystem instead of the legacy libSceNpTrophy2. Games like Onimusha: Way of the Sword now unlock correctly: the payload resolves each trophy's real unlock event from the game's own stats_extraction.json and lets the console's trophy daemon perform the award with a real system notification. Newer TRPTITLE.DAT layouts are parsed correctly, trophy sets show your real PSN username instead of a hex user ID, and the list re-polls after an unlock so counts update automatically.

The saves list now shows each save's own icon, sce_bu_* backup twins are filtered out, and mount/unmount is hardened with atomic staged-image write-back. A power-sensor buffer overflow is fixed — sceKernelGetSocPowerConsumption fills 0x70 bytes but was handed a 4-byte slot, overflowing ~108 bytes into adjacent statics on every poll. The SoC power reading now reports the sum of all 8 rails. The Android APK ships directly as PS5Suite.apk. Requires the v7.6.0 payload.

title: RetroArch v3.0.0-beta-3: Game Forwarder, SwanStation and melonDS DS cores
summary: PS5 RetroArch beta-3 adds Game Forwarder for home screen tiles, two new cores (SwanStation for PS1, melonDS DS with DualSense mic and touchpad), and Frame Generation pacing.
body: PS5 RetroArch v3.0.0-beta-3 lands three community contributions tested on a Base PS5. Game Forwarder lets you put any game from your library on the home screen as its own tile with its picture and name, using new --rom, --core and --exit-after-game launch options. Two new cores arrive: SwanStation brings a second PlayStation core drawing with Vulkan, and melonDS DS adds a second Nintendo DS core that maps the DualSense microphone to the DS mic and the touchpad to the stylus.

Frame Generation pacing ensures each game frame is shown exactly once on 60 Hz outputs and toggling Frame Generation on or off takes effect instantly. RetroAchievements now work with CHD disc images whose audio is compressed with FLAC. Content folders follow ES-DE system names. Requires etaHEN. No games, BIOS files or firmware are included — use only legally obtained backups of games you own.

title: PS5 Upload v7.1.3–v7.1.4: unified Payloads screen, HearBridge and file editing
summary: PS5 Upload v7.1.3 adds an "On your PS5" tab to manage running payloads, integrates HearBridge Bluetooth audio, and brings file permissions, text editing and uploads to PS5Upload Files.
body: PS5 Upload v7.1.3 redesigns the Payloads screen into three tabs: Catalog, Send and On your PS5. The new tab shows every payload running or installed on the console with status cards and actions — Open, Update when a newer release is out, and Stop. HearBridge cards display the connected headset, battery, link quality, latency, volume and game profile, with controls for volume, mute, reconnect, headset switching, night mode, latency and scan. A new Ports tab beside Processes shows which ports are open on the console and what listens there.

PS5Upload Files gains a permissions editor (owner/group/others or numeric like 755), new file creation and a text editor for files up to 1 MiB with safe atomic saves. When accessed from another device, Files supports uploading files and folders to the console and downloading files or entire folders as .tar archives, with skip/replace/keep-both conflict handling. v7.1.4 is a follow-up fix release.

title: ProsperoStore v1.000.090: catalog mirror fallback when the main site is blocked
summary: ProsperoStore v1.000.090 adds an automatic catalog mirror that kicks in when prosperostore.net is unreachable, with signature verification to block tampered or stale catalogs.
body: ProsperoStore v1.000.090 brings back the catalog mirror as a fallback for networks that block prosperostore.net. When the main site can't be reached, the store switches to a mirror hosted at darkxex.github.io. The mirror is trusted only as far as it verifies: its catalog must carry the same signature as the main site's, and a block page or an older unsigned catalog is refused. Only the exact catalog path on that host is accepted — addresses that climb out of it are blocked.

The update-check system for apps listed in the catalog can now use the mirror too. Still marked as an alpha release. Update from inside the store when it asks on launch, or install manually by unzipping PPSA99000.zip and replacing the PPSA99000 folder. If the console reports CE-107750-0, see the install note in the README.

title: Prospero Themes 01.000.007–008: category filters and snappier Community tab
summary: Prospero Themes adds browsable category filters (Anime, Games, Sci-Fi and more) to the Community tab and makes switching sort or category instant instead of waiting for images to load.
body: Prospero Themes 01.000.007 adds category filtering to the Community tab. Thirteen categories are available — Anime, Games, Movies & TV, Cartoon, Nature, Space, Fantasy, Sci-Fi, Pixel art, Minimal, Abstract and Seasonal — shown as chips next to the sort control. Each theme card shows up to three category badges, and theme authors pick their categories when publishing through the web creator. The header line updates to show the filter, like "12 themes · Anime · Top rated".

Version 01.000.008 makes the Community tab snappier: switching sort or category no longer waits for all images to finish loading. Download and Like actions now work while pictures are still loading instead of showing "Please wait". Tested on FW 13.00. Install by extracting PPSA90210.zip and copying the PPSA90210 folder to /data/homebrew/ on the console. ShadowMountPlus registers it. Requires an ELF loader on port 9021 (elfldr).

title: ShadowPKG v1.0.57: editable game libraries from Settings
summary: ShadowPKG v1.0.57 lets you add and edit game libraries directly from the Settings screen.
body: ShadowPKG v1.0.57 adds the ability to add and edit game libraries from the Settings screen. Previously, library paths had to be configured through other means; now you can manage them in one place within the app's own interface.

ShadowPKG is a self-hosted PKG manager that discovers and installs packages on jailbroken PS5 consoles over the local network. Update through your existing ShadowPKG instance or grab the release from GitHub.

title: PS5 Backport GUI 0.3.2: fixes false "not enough space" error
summary: PS5 Backport GUI 0.3.2-beta fixes the free-space check that was incorrectly reporting insufficient disk space even with 40+ GB available.
body: PS5 Backport GUI 0.3.2-beta is a small fix-up release that corrects the free-space check introduced in 0.3.1. Some testers were seeing "Not enough free space for the backport engine's working files" even with 40+ GB free on bigger games. The space calculation is now more accurate.

Everything from 0.3.1 is still included — the PS5 Pro PSSR 2 test, the backport engine and all previous features. Windows 10/11 x64 only for now; Linux and macOS will follow once Windows test results are satisfactory. Download PS5BackportGUI.exe and verify its SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS.txt.

title: WelcomeHubActivator: enable the PS5 Welcome Hub on firmware 10.00–13.60
summary: WelcomeHubActivator is an ELF payload that enables the PS5's Welcome Hub feature on jailbroken consoles running firmware 10.00 through 13.60.
body: WelcomeHubActivator by ghost1372 is an ELF payload that turns on the PS5's Welcome Hub, the content discovery screen Sony introduced in firmware 10.00. The payload supports firmware 10.00 through 13.60 and creates a backup of app.db before making changes. After running the payload and signing out and back in, the Welcome Hub appears on the home screen.

Before using it, you need to perform fake account activation and fake sign-in using ProsperoManager. If Welcome Hub fails to activate, a System Feature Update (not a regular firmware update) may be needed — the README explains how to install one without accidentally updating your firmware. The project is open-source and compiles against the PS5 Payload SDK.

title: SvR2008-Recomp-PS5: WWE SmackDown vs. Raw 2008 runs natively on PS5
summary: A PS5 port of nefariousjosiah's Xbox 360 recompilation of WWE SmackDown vs. Raw 2008, running at 60 fps with up to 4K resolution and PlayStation button prompts.
body: SvR2008-Recomp-PS5 by elripalda brings WWE SmackDown vs. Raw 2008 to the PS5 as a native homebrew app (PPSA92008). It's built on nefariousjosiah's WWE-SVR2008-RECOMP static recompilation and the ReXGlue SDK, drawing through Vulkan on the PS5's Mesa RADV driver. The game runs at 60 fps using the game's own 60 fps mode with resolution options of 720p, 1440p and 4K with anisotropic filtering. All Xbox button pictures are replaced with PlayStation equivalents, and the controller on superstar select screens is a DualSense.

A hub screen provides settings, save management with backups, and an Unlock Everything toggle that opens all superstars, legends, arenas and WWE Shop items without modifying your save. You need your own Xbox 360 disc image (.iso) — no game files are included. Install through RecompStore or manually by placing the app in /data/homebrew/PPSA92008/. Requires a jailbroken PS5 with a homebrew launcher.

title: PS5-Suite v7.5.0: File Manager gets create folder, chmod, and Android app
summary: PS5-Suite v7.5.0 overhauls the File Manager with folder creation, a chmod dialog, properties, path copying, terminal access and sorting, and brings the Android client to working status.
body: PS5-Suite v7.5.0 adds a full right-click context menu to the File Manager on all platforms: Create Folder, Change Permissions (a proper chmod dialog with R/W/X checkboxes for Owner/Group/Others synced with an octal field), Properties (size, type, permissions, timestamps), Copy Path, Open Terminal Here, Download Selected (multi-select) and Refresh. A new permissions column shows octal modes for every file and folder, and Sort By lets you order by name, size or date. The PS5 payload gains a native CMD_CHMOD command and extended directory listings that carry permission bits.

The Android app now actually works — the shared UI was refactored from Window to UserControl to fit Android's single-view lifetime, dialogs became cross-platform overlay cards, and the theme was corrected. A hardware bug was also fixed: ioctl 0x8001950e was the beeper's OFF setting, not an LED flag, so every colour change was silently muting the console beep. Requires the v7.5.0 payload (ps5_suite_server.elf); the updated LIST_DIR format is not backward-compatible.

title: PSBox Cloud Gaming v1.2.0: pristine 1080HQ streaming and DualSense haptics
summary: PSBox Cloud Gaming v1.2.0 delivers rock-solid 30 Mbps 1080HQ streaming with zero microstutter, audio bufferbloat elimination, DualSense adaptive triggers and audio-to-haptics vibration.
body: PSBox Cloud Gaming v1.2.0 validates a 30 Mbps REMB ceiling for crystal-clear 1080HQ visuals with zero dropped frames and 22 ms display latency, plus expanded bitrate options from 5 to 30 Mbps. A fast-forward video backlog drain eliminates microstutter caused by network jitter — recovery latency drops from 450+ ms to roughly 15 ms. Audio bufferbloat is fixed by bounding the audio queue to 80 ms and conditioning Opus packet-loss concealment to genuine loss only, cutting 300–700 ms audio chops to zero.

New PS5 hardware optimizations include Navi 21 Direct Hardware Blit (bypasses compute shaders at native 1080p, GPU draw time under 0.3 ms) and Zen 2 core pinning for decode and presentation threads. DualSense adaptive triggers get Light/Medium/Hard/Game-specific profiles, and real-time audio-to-haptics vibration synthesis feeds the controller's haptic motor. A modular in-game HUD lets you pick which statistics to show, and sign-in resilience handles restricted storage paths with automatic fallbacks.

sources.name: PSBox Cloud Gaming v1.2.0 on GitHub

title: PS5 Upload v7.1.2: multi-user save management on shared consoles
summary: PS5 Upload v7.1.2 adds per-user save labels and backup folders so shared PS5 consoles can track whose save data belongs to whom.
body: PS5 Upload v7.1.2 reworks save-data handling for shared PS5 consoles. Each save is now labelled with its owner's name instead of a number, and the screen starts on the user currently signed in at the console. A "Whose saves" button switches to another user or to everyone, and Back Up All / Restore All act on whichever saves are shown.

Backups are now organized per user: a PC backup is named after the game and the user (e.g. PPSA01234-Alice.zip), and USB backups go into per-user folders (<game>/<name>-<user id>/<date>/). Previously all users shared one folder per game, which meant "Restore all from USB" could overwrite one user's save with another's. Existing backups are still used when only one user on the console has a save of that game.

title: PS5 Backport GUI 0.3.1-beta: audio and crash fixes for multiple games
summary: PS5 Backport GUI 0.3.1-beta fixes missing audio in Story of Seasons and Wonderboy Asha, a Mewgenics crash on older firmware, and a Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 black screen on 4.xx.
body: PS5 Backport GUI's 0.3.1 testing build fixes no audio in STORY OF SEASONS: Grand Bazaar and WONDERBOY Asha in Monster World — other games hitting the same audio problem should also be fixed. Mewgenics crashing on boot on older firmware and KINGDOM HEARTS HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue showing a black screen or crash on 4.xx firmware are also resolved. All three fixes were tested on a base PS5 running firmware 4.50.

Everything from 0.3.0 remains, including the experimental PS5 Pro PSSR 2 option. To pick up the fixes, you need to rebuild your backport from the original game files with this version — old ZIPs will not change on their own. Download PS5BackportGUI.exe, verify its SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS.txt, and run it on Windows 10/11 x64. Bug reports go to GitHub Issues with firmware, console model, game PPSA/version, Export logs ZIP and ideally a klog.

title: PS5 Homebrew Tools: diagnostic payloads for process, thread and kernel inspection
summary: A new open-source toolkit offers process snapshots, thread probes, kstuff log decoding, kernel-text capture and a native app starter for PS5 homebrew developers.
body: PS5 Homebrew Tools is a new diagnostic suite by ShaneBreazeale aimed at PS5 homebrew developers. It includes payloads for process snapshots (one-shot or three-minute watch with birth, disappearance and zombie tracking), thread probes (raw sysctl records and per-process kernel thread records on firmware 13.60), a resident snapshot tool that reads counters and event rings from an instrumented kstuff resident, and kernel-text capture tools for bounded captures on PS5 Pro.

The project also provides host utilities for sending payloads, preserving raw output, log decoding and binary analysis, plus a minimal payload template to start your own diagnostic. Builds require Python 3.9+, the PS5 Payload SDK and LLVM 18 (a Docker reproducible build is also available). Note that built payloads still need console validation — this is source and local build tooling based on PS5 Pro firmware 13.60 research.

title: WebKit heap overflow demonstrated on PS5 firmware 14.10
summary: A researcher has demonstrated a working WebKit heap overflow on PS5 firmware 14.10, where all Relapse exploit bugs are patched. Kernel exploit work has not started yet.
body: Security researcher pastawithpesto has published a WebKit jailbreak research project targeting PS5 firmware 14.10, confirming a working heap overflow in JavaScriptCore on the console. The bug (JSC Bug 317632) is an integer overflow in UnlinkedMetadataTable::finalize() — 38.3 million call sites wrap an unsigned accumulator, causing the interpreter to allocate a 100 KB buffer but write 4.29 GB forward into heap memory. A bait-and-switch heap groom controls where the write lands, and probes have confirmed JSString object corruption with controllable .length values. All Relapse WebKit bugs were tested and found to be patched on 14.10.

This is early-stage research: the WebKit bug gives a heap primitive, but a kernel exploit has not been started. The project includes 14 probe results and device fingerprinting data from a real PS5 running firmware 14.10. The researcher notes that WebAssembly and SharedArrayBuffer are unavailable on the PS5 browser, and JIT is disabled (LLInt only). All data comes from on-device probes, with the open-source WebKit-1200 snapshot used as a structure reference.

title: VLC v0.4.5: VP9 hardware decoding, universal search and frame-rate matching
summary: VLC for PS5 v0.4.5 adds hardware-accelerated VP9 playback up to 4K HDR, a live search that covers videos, music, shares and 11,000+ free TV channels, and frame-rate matching for films.
body: VLC v0.4.5 brings VP9 hardware decoding to the PS5, so 4K VP9 videos (8-bit and 10-bit HDR) now play on the console's video chip instead of software decoding. A new universal search (R3 or Options menu, available from anywhere in the app including during playback) shows results as you type across your videos, music, playlists, network shares, 11,000+ free TV channels and radio stations. Match frame rate (off by default) switches the TV to the film's native refresh — 23.976, 24, 25 or 50 fps — so movies play without judder.

The update also speeds up software decoding by removing an unnecessary CPU resize step, fetches live TV segments over parallel connections, and fixes a long list of issues: a crash when opening Free TV after searching, IPTV stutter with hardware decoding on interlaced channels, search returning nothing in the Free TV list, videos freezing for up to 10 seconds after leaving a live channel, and several hardware decoding glitches with VP9 and HEVC. Requires kstuff and ShadowMountPlus.

title: ProsperoEden v1.005.000: game folders, cheat list, MihawkGen frame generation and speed control
summary: ProsperoEden v1.005.000 organises each game in its own folder, gives cheats a dedicated list, adds MihawkGen neural frame generation, and lets you run games faster than real time.
body: ProsperoEden v1.005.000 reorganises game storage so each title lives in its own folder under roms/, together with its updates, DLC, mods, cheats and post-processing presets. Cheats get their own list in each game's settings (separate from mods), and games can carry their own ReShade FX presets alongside the shared ones. A new speed limit setting (100%, 150%, 200%, 300% or Unlimited) lets games run faster when the console has headroom. MihawkGen, a neural-network frame generation method, joins Lossless Scaling as a selectable frame generation method per game.

The update also fixes a crash caused by GPU submissions growing too large during loading (the graphics driver now splits them), and a visual glitch where invalid colour values spread through glow and blur effects until black boxes covered the screen. Games requesting a large GPU address space no longer fail at startup. An Update notices toggle in Diagnostics lets you suppress the version check dialog. Requires kstuff and ShadowMountPlus.

title: PatchDL v0.3.0: pick any game update version and bypass blocked DNS
summary: PatchDL v0.3.0 lets you browse and download any available game patch version, bypasses blocked DNS with encrypted fallbacks, and adds 10 interface languages.
body: PatchDL v0.3.0 adds an Other Versions button to every game card, listing every patch that Prospero Patches (PS5) or Orbis Patches (PS4) knows for the game, with size and required firmware. Versions compatible with your console appear at the top, ready to download. The update also makes downloads more resilient: PatchDL now performs its own DNS lookups and falls back to encrypted DNS (Cloudflare, Google) or cached addresses when the console's DNS is blocked, so the DNS block that prevents system updates stays in place while game patches still download. Broken connections resume where they stopped, and queuing more than 16 games no longer stalls.

The interface now speaks English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Korean and Russian, following the browser language or a manual choice in Settings. Game cards show installed, update and newest versions side by side with larger text. Runs on firmware 1.00 to 13.60, tested on 11.60. Download patchdl_0.3.0.elf and send it to your PS5's ELF loader.

title: mupen64plus 0.7.5: find and create your own cheats on the PS5
summary: mupen64plus for PS5 0.7.5 adds a cheat search that lets you find memory values in any game and make custom GameShark codes, plus manual code entry from the on-screen keyboard.
body: mupen64plus 0.7.5 adds a cheat search to the pause menu that lets you hunt for values in a running game — lives, health, money — and turn them into custom cheats. Search for a known value or scan without one for things like health bars, then play, pause and narrow down results by what changed (went up, went down, stayed the same). Once you have a match, lock it at the value you want or set it once. The search works on 8, 16 and 32-bit values, and Undo takes back a step. You can also type GameShark codes directly with the PS5's on-screen keyboard.

Custom cheats appear first in the Cheats list, are saved per game in /data/mupen64plus/cheats/<game>.custom.txt (editable from a PC too), and can be renamed, edited or deleted with Square. The Cheats page now appears for every game, even those with no built-in codes. The touchpad returns to the game from any pause menu page.

title: Jobee'sLair v0.3.0: browser-based file capture, TorBox integration and host learning
summary: Jobee'sLair v0.3.0 captures download links from the PS5 browser automatically, adds TorBox as a debrid provider, and learns which file hosts work on your console.
body: Jobee'sLair v0.3.0 adds a browser capture feature that removes the need to type file links with the controller. When a download host requires the console's browser to pass a check, the app catches the file link out of the browser on its own, verifies it matches the game (by title ID or file size), and starts the download. VikingFile support is back as the catalog's largest host, and FileKeeper downloads work with no browser step at all. A new TorBox integration (add your API key in Settings) lets TorBox-supported sources download directly in the app, with Instant badges for files TorBox already has cached.

The app now remembers which hosts work on your console: successful captures mark a host Auto-capture and rank it first, while hosts that keep failing are marked Rarely works here and ranked last. Each source shows compatibility badges including whether it runs on 13.60 with ShadowMount+, and fPKG packages are labelled with their firmware ceiling. A download speed limit (no limit, 25, 10 or 5 MB/s) can be set in Settings. Link health checks no longer hide sources — broken or offline links are tagged and ranked last but remain available.

title: RecompStore v1.1.1–v1.1.2: original Xbox disc fix and reliable beta downloads
summary: Two quick RecompStore updates fix original Xbox disc setup (v1.1.1) and beta game downloads that could stall (v1.1.2), and add partial disc support for multi-game collections.
body: RecompStore v1.1.1 fixes setup for original Xbox game discs. The previous version only accepted Xbox 360 disc images, so an original Xbox .xiso.iso or full disc image was rejected with a missing default.xex error. If a game like Def Jam: Fight for NY failed to set up, update the store and try Set up game files again. Version 1.1.2 follows with fixes for beta game downloads that could sit on the download screen with an empty bar — beta zips now download in 4 MB chunks with per-chunk timeouts and automatic resume.

Version 1.1.2 also adds partial disc support: a game can take just its own folder from a multi-game disc collection. Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 3 copies only Budokai 3 from the Budokai HD Collection, skipping Budokai 1 and the collection menu. The store checks the disc's region first, so a disc from another region is rejected before anything is copied. Game updates now preserve your saves, settings and game files. Requires kstuff and ShadowMountPlus 1.7 Beta 5 or newer.

title: PS5 Backport GUI 0.3.0-beta: PS5 Pro PSSR 2 test and conversion fixes
summary: PS5 Backport GUI's latest testing build adds an experimental PS5 Pro PSSR 2 option and test fixes for games whose right.sprx fails conversion.
body: PS5 Backport GUI's early testing beta from 18 October 2026 (build 0.3.0-beta) adds an experimental PS5 Pro PSSR 2 test. The new option builds a Pro-only ZIP for games that use PSSR, letting the game select its requested PSSR model and permitting the system PSSR upgrade on Pro firmware 9.x–12.x. A row-menu action can also generate a PSSR 2 test from an existing backport without the original game files. This has not been tested on a PS5 Pro yet — tester reports are needed.

The build also tests fixes for several games (MGS4, 007 First Light, Planet of Lana) whose sce_sys/about/right.sprx fails conversion with an invalid param magic error, by replacing that file with a standard copy. The application remains closed source and Windows only, with Linux and macOS builds planned once Windows testing is confirmed. Base PS5 consoles do not run PSSR and should use the normal firmware 4.xx ZIP.

title: PS5 Upload v7.1.1: macOS Big Sur scroll fix
summary: PS5 Upload v7.1.1 fixes a scrolling issue on macOS Big Sur where the older WebKit engine prevented the app window from scrolling.
body: PS5 Upload v7.1.1 is a compatibility fix for macOS Big Sur. The older built-in web engine on Big Sur caused the app window to lose its fixed height, preventing all screens from scrolling, and the sidebar rows lost their left padding. The app's styles now include the older CSS forms that Big Sur's engine understands.
This is a host-side (PC/Mac) fix only and does not change PS5 functionality. If you're not on macOS Big Sur, this update has no effect. Download from the GitHub release page.

title: fps60: unlock 60 FPS in PS4 and PS5 games with one switch per game
summary: fps60 is a new payload that patches frame-rate limits in installed games on a jailbroken PS5, controllable from a web page on the TV or your phone.
body: fps60 is a payload for jailbroken PS5 that scans your installed games, matches them against a built-in database of roughly 160 community frame-rate patches (sourced from illusion0001's PS4-PS5-Game-Patch collection), and lets you toggle 60 FPS unlocks per game from a web page served on the console's browser or any device on your network. When a patched game launches, fps60 writes the patch into game memory as it loads — your game files are never modified, and switches are saved across reboots. The interface shows whether each patch matches your installed game version, and an Activity log tracks every apply and error. Gravity Rush 2 and The Order: 1886 are confirmed working on a real PS5 so far.

fps60 requires a jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader on port 9021 (Relapse, etaHEN or Payload Manager). Send fps60.elf to the console after jailbreaking, then open the fps60 tile from the Media row on the home screen or navigate to http://ps5-ip:8060 on a phone. Add it to Payload Manager's autoload list to start it automatically. Built with PS5 payload SDK v0.44 and reproducibly built through GitHub Actions.

title: PS5 Upload v7.1.0: full file manager on the TV
summary: PS5 Upload v7.1.0 adds PS5Upload Files, a controller-driven file manager that runs in the PS5 browser and fills the TV, plus fixes for large app databases hiding installed games.
body: PS5 Upload v7.1.0 introduces PS5Upload Files, a new tile on the PS5 home screen that opens a full file manager in the PS5 browser. The interface is built for the controller — X selects, Circle goes back, Triangle opens actions — and supports browsing, copying, cutting, pasting, renaming (including batch rename with patterns), deleting, creating folders, fixing permissions, searching across drives, viewing disk usage, and inspecting files (text with find, JSON, hex, pictures, game param.json summaries). It also lets you decompress .ffpfsc images with progress, verify files with BLAKE3 and CRC32, eject USB drives and unmount game images, and switch between Dark, Light, OLED and Peach themes. Cheats for the running game can be toggled from a dedicated tab. Files pinned on the console show up in the PC app and vice versa.

The update also fixes a bug where consoles with large app databases (over 256 entries) would hide some installed games. An optional "Allow other devices" setting lets a phone or computer on the same network open the file manager too — there is no password, so turn it off when done. Requires the PS5Upload helper to be loaded; the tile can be removed from Settings. Download from the GitHub release page.

title: RecompStore v1.1.0: beta game codes and log reporting
summary: RecompStore v1.1.0 adds a code redemption page for beta games and a Send Logs button on every game page for easier bug reporting.
body: RecompStore v1.1.0 introduces two features aimed at testing and troubleshooting. A new Redeem a Code page in Settings accepts codes in the 12-345-678 format to unlock games in testing — redeemed titles appear in your Library with a Beta tag. Every game page now also has a Send Logs button that sends the store log and game-specific logs along with an optional message, so developers can track down problems without asking users to dig through files. Saves and game files are not included in the report.

If you already have RecompStore installed, open the app and update from Latest Updates. For a fresh install, send the RecompStore-Installer.elf to your PS5 payload loader on port 9021. Requires kstuff and ShadowMountPlus 1.7 Beta 5 or newer. No game files are included — every game requires your own legally obtained copy.

title: ProsperoTube 1.000.010: Afterglow-only with non-Latin text and player fixes
summary: ProsperoTube 1.000.010 drops the Classic interface, fixes broken non-Latin text and scrambled thumbnails, and restores player features like Up Next and auto-captions.
body: ProsperoTube 1.000.010 makes Afterglow the only interface — the Classic browser view and its settings are gone, and if Afterglow fails to start a page offers to retry or close. Player actions like Open Channel, Search and Share now open the matching Afterglow page with Circle returning to where you were. Text in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari and other non-Latin scripts no longer renders as boxes or question marks, using the console's own fonts. Scrambled rainbow thumbnails are also fixed.

Several player features are restored: pressing Up turns on captions with the best available track including auto-translated ones, Up Next (Triangle) works for signed-in profiles with a retry on failure, the next video plays automatically when one ends (respecting your end-of-video mode), and descriptions, video details and live chat load again for signed-in accounts. Install by updating from within the app if listed on homebrew.page, or download PPSA99012.zip from the release page and copy to /data/homebrew/.

title: SwanStationPS5 1.4.2: drive validation for ext0/ext1 game folders
summary: SwanStationPS5 1.4.2 only creates and scans ext0 and ext1 game folders when the drive is readable with enough free space, and tidies up the About screen.
body: SwanStationPS5 1.4.2 tightens the handling of ext0 and ext1 game folders on external drives. These folders are now only created and searched for games when the drive passes the same health check used by the Drives list in About — it must be readable and have enough free space. This prevents errors or stalls when an unusable drive is connected. The update also removes the "Continuing where you left off..." notice that appeared when resuming a game.

The About screen now shows the full GitHub repository address under the QR code alongside the author's X page. SwanStationPS5 is a Vulkan-based PS1 emulator for jailbroken PS5 consoles with RetroAchievements support. Update by downloading the latest release from GitHub and copying the app folder to /data/homebrew/ on the console.

title: Prospero Themes 01.000.006: full UI redesign with glass panels and dialog prompts
summary: Prospero Themes 01.000.006 redesigns every screen with antialiased controls, glass-panel backgrounds, readable cards and dialog-based apply and restore prompts.
body: Prospero Themes 01.000.006 is a major visual overhaul. Buttons, badges and symbols are now antialiased, thumbnails are rounded and sharp, and every screen uses glass panels over a blurred background with a consistent focus ring and type scale. The header spaces tabs evenly with L1/R1 indicators and shows a spinner while the app works. The Library displays larger titles and descriptions with a "what it changes" line, an Applied badge on the active theme and a smoothly scrolling card row. The Details view fixes the old overlapping title and replaces raw file paths with a grouped list of what the theme changes (Background, App background, Icons, Tile icons and more). Apply and Restore now ask in a dialog with D-pad selection, X to confirm and Circle to cancel; themes with an app background prompt whether to apply it to apps without their own image or to all tiles. The Community tab gets readable cards with a sort control, scrolling grid and heart icons for liked themes. The System tab is reorganised into a PS5-style settings list.

Prospero Themes requires a jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader on port 9021 (elfldr). Update by extracting PPSA90210.zip and copying the PPSA90210 folder to /data/homebrew/ on the console; ShadowMountPlus registers it. Your library, backups and settings in /data/prospero-themes/ are preserved. Tested on firmware 13.00 at 60 fps; the theme-helper fix for 13.40 and later from 01.000.004 is included.

title: ProsperoMenu: Tesla-style overlay menu for jailbroken PS5
summary: ProsperoMenu brings a community-expandable overlay system to jailbroken PS5 consoles, drawn natively by ShellUI and accessible anywhere with L3 + R3.
body: ProsperoMenu is a new overlay menu for jailbroken PS5 inspired by the Switch's Tesla Menu. It docks to the left edge of the screen and is drawn by the PS5's own ShellUI, so it appears over the home screen, inside apps and during gameplay. Press L3 + R3 to open it; while open the game is paused and your controller is captured by the menu. Entries are community overlays: folders in /data/ProsperoMenu/overlays/ that anyone can write in C with the SDK or as a simple menu.json file and share by copying the folder. Built-in overlays include fan control, console tools and a games launcher. ProsperoMenu also supports custom boot animations (MP4 clips played on console start) and includes ProsperoSettings for theme colours, a colour picker, overlay management and a file browser.

ProsperoMenu is tested on firmware 13.60 and requires a jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader. It does not carry its own kstuff or ShadowMount — it finds the copies your autoloader already started. It also includes Elf-Updater to keep kstuff-lite, ShadowMountPlus and zftpd up to date from GitHub, and runs an FTP share on port 2122 for file transfers.

title: ShadowPKG v1.0.56: game covers on by default and CPU-temp toggle
summary: ShadowPKG v1.0.53–v1.0.56 add a CPU-temperature toggle, refine its scope and switch the Installed-list game covers on by default.
body: Four quick-fire updates land for the ShadowPKG package manager. Version 1.0.54 introduces a HEADER_TEMP console setting that lets you hide the CPU-temperature chip from the header and list; v1.0.55 narrows the toggle so only the header chip is hidden while the console list always displays it. Version 1.0.56 flips the covers toggle to on by default, so the Installed list shows each game’s icon out of the box without needing to opt in. A minor v1.0.53 tweak also moves the Settings button next to Done in the setup dialog header.

Update by downloading the latest release ZIP from GitHub and copying the extracted PPSA90211 folder to /data/homebrew/ on a jailbroken PS5 with an ELF loader on port 9021. ShadowMountPlus registers it automatically. Existing settings and library data are preserved.

title: ShadowPKG v1.0.52: drives view, CPU temp chip and zhttp installer detection
summary: ShadowPKG v1.0.50–1.0.52 replaces the file tree with a drives view in the System dialog, shows CPU temperature beside the selected console, and recognises zhttp-based installers in diagnostics.
body: ShadowPKG v1.0.50 reworks the System dialog to display drives instead of the raw file tree, and adds more patient temperature polling so the readout arrives reliably. Version 1.0.51 promotes the CPU temp chip to the header row beside the selected console, giving it a permanent spot without opening the System dialog. Version 1.0.52 tweaks diagnostics: a console whose DPI host is not answering but that runs zftpd's zhttp build is now correctly counted as having an installer, matching the recognition the /api/status endpoint already applies.

ShadowPKG is a self-hosted PKG manager that discovers and installs packages on jailbroken PS5 consoles over the local network. Update through your existing ShadowPKG instance or grab the release from GitHub.

title: Prospero Themes 01.000.005: FW 13.40+ fix and app-background placement choice
summary: Prospero Themes 01.000.004–005 fix the theme helper on firmware 13.40, 13.42 and 13.60, and let you choose whether an app-tile background applies to all apps or only those without their own image.
body: Version 01.000.004 fixes a critical bug that prevented the theme helper from starting on firmware 13.40 and later. The startup code inherited from SharpProspero was hard-coded to the 13.00 kernel offset for the process list; on 13.40, 13.42 and 13.60 it silently failed. The fix has been submitted upstream as SvenGDK/SharpProspero#6. Version 01.000.005 adds a placement prompt when applying a theme that includes an app-tile background: press X to apply the background only to apps without their own image, or Triangle to apply it to every app tile. Your choice is saved as the background scope on the System tab.

Install or update by extracting PPSA90210.zip and copying the PPSA90210 folder to /data/homebrew/ on the console. ShadowMountPlus registers it automatically. Your library, backups and settings in /data/prospero-themes/ are preserved. Requires a jailbroken PS5 and an ELF loader on port 9021. The FW 13.40+ fix is not yet hardware-verified — report results in the GitHub issue.

title: SwanStationPS5 1.4.1: NFS timeout tuning, reconnect retry and Nostalgia mode
summary: SwanStationPS5 1.4.1 adds a configurable NFS timeout, automatic reconnect on read failures, NFS share setup from the settings web page, and a new Nostalgia mode that silences all system overlays during gameplay.
body: SwanStationPS5 1.4.1 brings several NFS improvements: a new NFS timeout setting (5–30 seconds, default 15) replaces the old fixed 5-second limit, and a failed or stalled read is now retried on a fresh connection — the game pauses while reconnecting and a notice appears. NFS shares can also be configured from the settings web page. Text fields throughout the app now support up to 511 characters with scrolling and L1/R1 cursor movement. The headline addition is Nostalgia mode (Screen > Picture, off by default): while enabled, the emulator suppresses all sounds, trophies, notices and progress cards during gameplay, leaving only the game itself.

SwanStationPS5 is a Vulkan-based PS1 emulator for jailbroken PS5 consoles with RetroAchievements support. Update by downloading the latest release from GitHub and copying the app folder to /data/homebrew/ on the console.

title: Seedee5 v1.21: new logo and safer download redirects
summary: Seedee5 v1.21 gives the CD-i emulator a new S5 app icon and tightens download security by restricting redirect targets to trusted domains.
body: Seedee5 v1.21 introduces a new S5 logo that appears on the PS5 home screen, at the top left of the game wheel and on the project page. The other change is a security improvement: when downloading cover art or game information, Seedee5 now only follows HTTP redirects within the same site or to Wikipedia, GitHub and libretro. Redirects to any other address — including devices on your home network — are blocked, preventing potential abuse of open-redirect URLs in metadata sources.

Seedee5 is a native Philips CD-i emulator for jailbroken PS5 consoles (PPSA99142). Update by downloading Seedee5-1.21.zip, extracting the PPSA99142 folder and copying it over FTP to /data/homebrew/ on your PS5. Do not delete the old folder first — your saves and settings are preserved.

title: ProsperoStore v1.000.080: catalog now sorted into categories
summary: ProsperoStore v1.000.080 adds eleven browsable categories to the app catalog, splitting apps across shelves like Console game ports, Emulators, Music & audio and more.
body: ProsperoStore v1.000.080 introduces category browsing to the homebrew app catalog. Every listed app is now tagged with one of eleven categories: Console game ports, PC game ports, Homebrew games, Emulators, Game streaming, Video & TV, Music & audio, AI, Utilities, Tools & tests and Showcases. The Discover page shows a shelf per category in place of the old Apps, Games and Tools shelves, and inside each section you can press L2/R2 to step through the categories it holds. A separate "New in the catalog" shelf highlights apps listed in the last thirty days, while "Recently updated" now only flags apps whose developer has published a newer release after listing.

Update from inside the store when prompted on launch, or install manually by unzipping PPSA99000.zip and replacing the PPSA99000 folder on the console. If the console reports error CE-107750-0 after updating, consult the Install section in the project README. Requires a jailbroken PS5 with ShadowMountPlus. This is still an alpha release — report issues on GitHub.

title: Prospero Themes 01.000.003: multi-firmware support and firmware reports
summary: Prospero Themes 01.000.002–003 remove the firmware 13.00 restriction, add safe per-file validation before writing, and generate a firmware report for easier debugging on untested firmwares.
body: Prospero Themes 01.000.002 drops the hard dependency on firmware 13.00. Before writing any file, the app now backs up and compares every file a theme replaces against the console's own copy — checking texture size, format and image dimensions. Files that do not match are skipped and listed, never written; icons the console does not have are also skipped. When a system update replaces backed-up files, the app notices and adopts the new copies as defaults (old backups move to /data/prospero-themes/backup/replaced/), so "Restore defaults" never puts an outdated firmware file back. The System tab now shows the running firmware version.

Release 01.000.003 follows up with a firmware report that works even when the theme helper fails to start: the System tab's Options still saves /data/prospero-themes/reports/firmware-<version>.json, marking unreadable files rather than omitting them, so you can attach the report to an issue for Darkatek7. Install or update by extracting PPSA90210.zip to /data/homebrew/ on the console. Requires ShadowMountPlus and an ELF loader on port 9021.

title: Prospero Themes 01.000.001: theme update badges and version tracking
summary: Prospero Themes 01.000.001 adds version tracking in the Community tab so you can see when a theme creator publishes a new version of a pack you already have.
body: Prospero Themes 01.000.001 adds theme versioning to the Community tab. Each theme card now shows its version number, and when a creator publishes a new version of a theme you have downloaded, the card gets an orange Update badge. Tapping Update replaces the old version in your library while the previous pack is kept in /data/prospero-themes/attic/ as a backup. If the updated theme is currently applied, you need to apply it again to see the changes on your home screen.

Update by downloading the new PPSA90210.zip from the GitHub release, extracting the PPSA90210 folder to /data/homebrew/ on the console, and letting ShadowMountPlus register it. Your library, backups and settings in /data/prospero-themes/ are preserved across updates. Requires a jailbroken PS5 on firmware 13.00 and an ELF loader on port 9021.

title: Prospero Themes: a theme manager for the PS5 home screen
summary: Prospero Themes by Darkatek7 is a native homebrew app that lets you browse, download and apply theme packs to the PS5 home screen, with a community store and USB import.
body: Prospero Themes is a new PS5 homebrew app (PPSA90210) by Darkatek7 that manages theme packs for the home screen. A Library tab holds your installed .p5theme packs with fullscreen previews. The Community tab connects to themes.darkatek7.com where you can browse, sort by rating or downloads, and like community-made themes. USB Import checks a drive for packs and copies them into the library. Themes can change the home-screen background (including behind system tiles like Game Library and Media Gallery), app tile backgrounds, system icons and system tile icons. The app always starts from defaults before applying a theme, so they never stack, and a Restore Defaults option in the System tab puts every original file back.

The app requires a jailbroken PS5 on firmware 13.00, ShadowMountPlus to register apps from /data/homebrew/, and an ELF loader on port 9021. Install by downloading PPSA90210.zip from the GitHub release, extracting the folder to /data/homebrew/ on the console, and letting ShadowMountPlus register it. Your library, backups and settings are stored in /data/prospero-themes/ so updating the app keeps them. A web-based theme creator at themes.darkatek7.com lets you build and publish your own packs.

title: ShadowPKG v1.0.43: fixes console discovery on port 8888
summary: ShadowPKG v1.0.43 adds port 8888 to the FTP probe fallback list so profiles whose port drifted can rediscover a zhttp-only console automatically.
body: ShadowPKG v1.0.43 fixes a connectivity issue with zhttp-only consoles. When a console binds its HTTP API on port 8888, ShadowPKG's port probe could not find it because 8888 was missing from the ftpPortsOf fallback list. A profile whose saved port had drifted away from 8888 would never reconnect on its own. This update adds 8888 to the probe list so discovery self-corrects.

ShadowPKG is a self-hosted web app that reads .pkg files from folders you choose, lets you browse and search them from a phone or PC browser, and sends them to a PS5 over the network. It runs on Node or Docker. Update by pulling the latest release from GitHub.

title: Seedee5 v1.20: game info cards with Wikipedia descriptions and review scores
summary: Seedee5 v1.20 adds game cards that pull descriptions from Wikipedia and review scores from publications like AllGame, Edge and CD-i Magazine, plus cached artwork from libretro-thumbnails.
body: Seedee5 v1.20 introduces game cards that appear when you open a game. Each card shows a brief description sourced from the game's Wikipedia article (credited under CC BY-SA 4.0), review scores from publications where available (AllGame, Edge, CD-i Magazine, Next Generation and others), and a dimmed in-game screenshot backdrop with the game's own logo. Artwork and thumbnails come from the libretro-thumbnails collection. Everything is cached locally after the first view so cards open instantly offline, and the feature can be turned off in Settings.

The project has also been rebranded to Seedee5 with a new logo used as both the app icon and wheel graphic. A sound diagnostic now logs what the CD-i's sound chip played and whether it ran dry. Install by copying the PPSA99142 folder over FTP to /data/homebrew/ on a jailbroken PS5. When updating, copy over the existing folder to keep your saves and settings.

title: ps5-solobridge v0.1.1: fixes audio pitch shift on capture start
summary: ps5-solobridge v0.1.1 fixes a 2% pitch shift that occurred for about 17 seconds whenever a capture session started, and makes drift correction 8x gentler.
body: ps5-solobridge v0.1.1 fixes an audio pitch shift that affected the first 17 seconds after a capture session started — on payload launch or game switch, the backlog from the capture service was played about 2% faster than normal. The backlog is now skipped entirely, and ongoing drift corrections have been reduced to 0.26% (8x gentler than before). The status command also now shows the sample rate read back from the Scarlett Solo.

Tested on PS5 firmware 13.60 with a Focusrite Scarlett Solo 3rd gen. Install by sending solobridge.elf to your ELF loader on port 9021, or place it in /data/pldmgr/payloads/local/solobridge/ for Payload Manager. SHA-256 checksums and VirusTotal scan links are provided in the release.

title: Stream8: experimental hardware H.264 streaming from PS5 to browser
summary: Stream8 is an open-source PS5 payload that captures the console's composited video output using the hardware H.264 encoder and streams it at 720p60 to a browser over the local network.
body: Stream8 by psksuffsmp is an experimental payload for jailbroken PS5 on firmware 13.60 that streams the console's final video output to a PC browser over the local network. It injects into the SceGameLiveStreaming system process and captures hardware-encoded H.264 video at 1280×720 60 FPS, targeting up to 30 Mbps. The stream plays in Edge or Chrome via WebCodecs. Unlike Remote Play it does not send controller input — the DualSense stays connected directly to the console.

The project requires a jailbroken PS5 on firmware 13.60 with a payload loader, a firmware-compatible NineS ELF injector, Python 3 on the PC, and a wired LAN connection is strongly recommended. A PowerShell launcher automates the full startup sequence on Windows. Stream8 is currently experimental — it works with RDR2 but game-to-game switching is under investigation, there is no audio, and recovery requires a reboot. The payload contains firmware-specific offsets and must not be used on other firmware versions.

title: Seedee5: Philips CD-i emulator for PS5
summary: Seedee5 brings the SAME_CDI core (based on MAME) to the PS5 as a native homebrew title, with a cover-wheel library, game info cards, NAS support and picture filters for FMV games.
body: Seedee5 by mortaljinx is a native PS5 homebrew emulator for the Philips CD-i, built on the SAME_CDI core from MAME. It features a cover-wheel game browser with box art sorted A–Z, game info cards with review scores and playtime, and support for games stored on the console, a USB drive, or a NAS over NFS. Supported formats include .chd, .cue/.bin, .iso, and .7z archives. Games on a NAS are copied to the console when launched.

No games, BIOS files or keys are included — you need your own CD-i library. The emulator also includes picture filters designed for the CD-i’s full-motion-video titles. A jailbroken PS5 running homebrew is required.

title: MacheteSVG v1.3.0: native kernel SPRX loader and pre-format save injection
summary: MacheteSVG v1.3.0 fixes PS5 save restoration after a console format, adds a native kernel SPRX loader, and resolves PS4 backwards-compatible save loading.
body: MacheteSVG v1.3.0 (Build #55) resolves key edge cases in save management on real PS5 hardware running firmware 12.40. A SAMU key-decryption fix removes a false-negative check that was discarding valid AES PFS keys for PS5 sdimg containers, and the console’s OpenPSID is now retrieved directly from libkernel. The new native kernel SPRX loader uses sceKernelLoadStartModule and sceKernelDlsym directly from libkernel after privilege elevation, bypassing sandbox dlopen restrictions.

This release also adds PS5 pre-format save dummy injection, letting you restore backups that were created before the console was formatted. PS4 backwards-compatible saves now load inside games without triggering an error. Requires a jailbroken PS5 with homebrew support.

title: PatchDL v0.2.1: clear download failure messages and sideloaded app protection
summary: PatchDL v0.2.1 shows plain-language reasons when a download fails and leaves sideloaded apps alone by default.
body: PatchDL v0.2.1 improves error handling when game update downloads fail. The game card now shows exactly why a download could not start — server not found, connection failed, or a Sony server error — alongside a Details link that runs a connection check and produces a copyable report for GitHub issues. On the PS5 itself, a QR code lets you scan and copy the report on your phone.

The update also adds sideloaded app detection. Apps that are Sony-signed but installed outside the Store are now marked as Sideloaded with updates switched off by default, so Update All leaves them untouched. You can still enable updates for individual sideloaded apps if you want the newer version. Runs on firmware 1.00 to 13.60.

title: ps5-solobridge: route PS5 audio to a Focusrite Scarlett Solo over USB
summary: ps5-solobridge is a resident payload that sends the PS5’s game and system audio to a Focusrite Scarlett Solo 3rd-gen USB audio interface, bypassing the console’s UAC1-only restriction.
body: ps5-solobridge by hebiii994 is a resident payload for jailbroken PS5 that routes both game and system audio to a Focusrite Scarlett Solo 3rd-gen connected over USB. The PS5 normally only accepts USB Audio Class 1 devices, but the Scarlett Solo is UAC2-only, so the console ignores it. This payload drives the Solo directly through FreeBSD’s /dev/ugen interface and captures the console mix from the system capture service, adding roughly 16–40 ms of latency.

The payload is resident, surviving unplugs and game switches. Audio keeps playing on HDMI simultaneously. A TCP control port provides status and stop commands. Tested on firmware 13.60 with a Scarlett Solo 3rd gen. Install by sending solobridge.elf to your ELF loader.

title: ProsperoEden v1.004.000: post-processing looks, custom wallpapers and smarter memory
summary: The Switch emulator for PS5 adds six ReShade-based visual presets, user-importable wallpapers, and a memory system that frees hundreds of megabytes during gameplay.
body: ProsperoEden v1.004.000 adds a post-processing pipeline built on ReShade FX effects. Six presets ship with the app — Anime, Cinematic, Clean, Dreamy, Retro and Vivid — and you can drop your own presets and shaders into the user folders over FTP. A new wallpaper setting lets you place your own PNG or JPEG behind the launcher screens. The emulator also now keeps the graphics driver's compiled shaders between launches, so games with thousands of pipelines no longer stall during loading and start faster on every subsequent run.

The headline technical change is how the emulator handles the emulated console's memory. RAM is now allocated only where a game writes it and released where the game frees it or leaves it zeroed, saving 644 to 1,956 MiB in two tested games. An optional Compact Memory setting reclaims a further 100 to 300 MiB by giving back mostly-empty pages, though it can cause stuttering in games that keep rewriting them. Other improvements include game language detection from packed updates, scrollable public rooms, self-updating launcher packs and crash reports that name the allocation that failed.

title: PSBox Cloud Gaming v1.1.0: Linux preview and PS5 microphone fix
summary: The Xbox Cloud Gaming client ships a Linux build for the first time, alongside a fix for the PS5 microphone gain that was silencing players at the default setting.
body: PSBox Cloud Gaming v1.1.0 adds a preview Linux build for x86-64 desktops. The Linux version supports fullscreen and windowed modes, DualSense adaptive triggers, light bar, gyro aiming and touchpad, plus Xbox and generic controllers with Xbox button glyphs. Keyboard, mouse, sound and microphone all work. The picture filters — FSR, Anime4K, sharpening and block smoothing — are not yet available on Linux.

On PS5, this release fixes a microphone gain bug where the 50% setting silently muted the mic and 150% gave double the expected volume. Under the hood, the app core is now shared across every platform. The PS5 app behaviour is unchanged and was verified on console across every screen and during streaming. DualSense features on Linux need read/write access to the controller's hidraw device, which most desktop environments grant by default.

title: PS5 Upload v7.0.34: Unity games no longer crash when uploaded as folders
summary: A case-sensitivity fix stops Unity-based games from crashing seconds after launch when they're uploaded or converted as folders instead of exFAT images.
body: PS5 Upload v7.0.34 fixes a crash that hit Unity-based games running from folders on the PS5's internal storage. Some game dumps spell a key file as Il2cppUserAssemblies.prx, but the game engine loads it as Il2CppUserAssemblies.prx with different capitalisation. An exFAT image ignores the difference, so these games worked fine from a .exfat file. The console's internal filesystem does not — the same game uploaded as a folder, or converted to one, crashed within a second of launching.

The fix applies when uploading a game folder and when using Convert's game-folder and .ffpkg outputs. Each affected file is quietly renamed to the spelling the game expects. The original copy on your computer is left unchanged, and Convert's checks list what was renamed. The developer confirmed the fix on a PS5 Pro running firmware 13.60.

title: DevilutionX brings Diablo and Hellfire to PS5 with Vulkan rendering
summary: An unofficial PS5 build of the DevilutionX source port runs Diablo and its Hellfire expansion natively on jailbroken consoles, with DualSense button prompts and resolutions up to 1080p.
body: DevilutionX, the open-source reverse-engineered port of Blizzard's original Diablo, now runs on jailbroken PS5 as an installed homebrew title. Built by griches — the developer behind Ghostship (Super Mario 64), Wind Waker HD, Super Mario Sunshine, Dusklight (Twilight Princess), Doom 3 BFG and Quake III ports — it uses SDL3's Vulkan renderer through the PS5's RADV driver stack. The game supports controller, keyboard and mouse input, with DualSense button prompts shown in-game. Resolution options include 1080p, 720p, 540p and 480p, defaulting to 960×540. Save and load work, and settings persist between sessions.
